item.title: What happened when I raised the price
item.description: Raising $29 to $39 with grandfathering lost nobody; the new price only ever applied to people who never saw the old one.
item.dc:creator: tidewell lore
item.content:encoded:
Raising $29 to $39 with grandfathering lost nobody; the new price only ever applied to people who never saw the old one.

I braced for cancellations and got two thank-you notes. The trick was not cleverness, it was order: existing groomers were told first and kept their price, and new visitors never saw $29 at all.

item.title: Twilio, Stripe and the boring middle
item.description: Most of Tidewell is the boring middle between a text message and a payout: Twilio sends the reminder, Stripe Connect Express moves the money, and a small Django app keeps the two honest.
item.dc:creator: tidewell lore
item.content:encoded:
Most of Tidewell is the boring middle between a text message and a payout: Twilio sends the reminder, Stripe Connect Express moves the money, and a small Django app keeps the two honest.

Nobody asks about that middle until it breaks, so it gets a checklist, a dashboard and an on-call phone that is always on the passenger seat.

item.title: A week in the van with Delia
item.description: I spent a week riding along in Delia's grooming van, notebook in hand, watching where the software helped and where it got in the way.
item.dc:creator: tidewell lore
item.content:encoded:
I spent a week riding along in Delia's grooming van, notebook in hand, watching where the software helped and where it got in the way.

On Tuesday the route sent us to the wrong side of a rail crossing. On Thursday a customer's dog would not leave the porch and the whole afternoon slid twenty minutes. Every problem I wrote down that week became a line on the roadmap.

item.title: The deposit that fixed no-shows
item.description: A 25 % no-show deposit cut no-shows from 18 % to 4 % in six weeks.
item.dc:creator: tidewell lore
item.content:encoded:
A 25 % no-show deposit cut no-shows from 18 % to 4 % in six weeks.

Delia was losing about one booking in five to people who simply did not answer the door. We asked new customers for a quarter of the price at booking time, credited it against the final bill, and refunded it automatically if the groomer cancelled.

Repeat customers never noticed, because they are exempt after their second visit.
